lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: Ajax — you went mad and killed yourself. You also came very close to killing the rest of us. Why are you still blaming Odysseus? The other day, when he came down to consult the oracle, you wouldn't even look at him. You wouldn't speak to a fellow soldier, a comrade — you just went striding past with your nose in the air.
lines.description: weary commander, controlled reproach with dry disbelief

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: With good reason, Agamemnon. He is the sole cause of my madness — the one man who stood against me for the armour.
lines.description: tight fury, grievance kept burning for eternity

lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: And you expected to walk off with it unopposed? To beat everyone without breaking a sweat?
lines.description: dry incredulity, senior officer testing the absurdity

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: Yes. In a matter like that — yes. The armour was practically family property. He was my cousin. The rest of you — all of you better men than Odysseus — declined the contest and stepped aside for me. But the son of Laertes — whom I personally rescued, more than once, when the Phrygians were about to cut him to pieces — he decided he was the better man. He decided the armour suited him better.
lines.description: righteous and wounded, building into bitter contempt

lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: Then blame Thetis, my good fellow. She should have handed the armour straight to you — you were the relative. Instead she tossed it into open competition.
lines.description: pragmatic, mildly sardonic attempt to redirect blame

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: No. I blame Odysseus. He was the only one who contested it.

lines.speaker: Agamemnon
lines.text: Forgive him, Ajax. He's a man. He wanted glory — the sweetest thing there is. Every one of us faced death for it. And he did beat you, you know. In front of Trojan judges, no less.
lines.description: patient mediation, then a dry needle at the end

lines.speaker: Ajax
lines.text: I know exactly who condemned me. But one mustn't speak ill of the gods. [pause] As for Odysseus — I could not stop hating him, Agamemnon. Not if Athena herself ordered me to.
lines.description: darkly restrained, then absolute hatred after the pause
